#6144. Last-minute strategies for earning Delta Medallion elite status

With just two months left in 2026, time is running out to qualify (or requalify) for Delta Medallion elite status.

If you have not done so already, check your elite qualification metrics, tally up your travel for the rest of the year and see where that puts you in terms of elite status for next year. If you're short of your goal, you still have time to close the gap. There are plenty of ways to earn Delta status — and they don't all involve flying.

Here are some ideas to help you earn what you need by the end of the year and reap the benefits of Medallion status in 2027.

Related: Reciprocal earning coming soon from new Delta-Hyatt partnership

Remember that as of Jan. 1, 2024, Delta consolidated all Medallion status earning activities into Medallion Qualification Dollars, axing Medallion Qualification Miles and Medallion Qualification Segments.

Now, flyers earn MQDs not just on eligible travel purchases with Delta and its partners, but also on other activities, such as spending on Delta-issued credit cards and vacation packages. You'll need to reach the following MQD thresholds for each Medallion status tier:

Of course, the most obvious route to status is by booking paid flights through Delta: You'll earn 1 MQD per dollar on the ticket price of any Delta-marketed flight operated by Delta or its partner airlines (except in basic economy, which doesn't earn miles or MQDs). However, Delta's new "basic" premium fares still earn MQDs.

However, there are plenty of other ways to earn MQDs without setting foot on an airplane. Here are some last-minute strategies to help put you over the top for Delta elite status in 2026.

One of the best changes to the SkyMiles program in recent years is that Delta award tickets booked in Main Cabin or higher now earn MQDs. This can make earning status much cheaper.

If you have a stash of SkyMiles in your account, consider redeeming them to close the gap to your desired status tier. The number of MQDs you'll earn is calculated by dividing the number of miles redeemed by 100. (And remember, holders of select Delta American Express cards automatically save 15% on Delta-operated award tickets.)

There is one major exception to keep in mind: Only Delta-ticketed award flights earn MQDs. Your award ticket must be booked with Delta SkyMiles through a direct Delta channel in order to qualify (though it does not need to be operated by Delta). For example, using Air France-KLM Flying Blue miles to book an award flight operated by Delta won't earn MQDs, even if you add your SkyMiles number to the itinerary.

Related: Your complete guide to the Delta SkyMiles program

Since achieving Delta Medallion status now requires hitting spending thresholds, mileage runs are not the useful tool they once were if you're flying on Delta metal. On the bright side, you can still leverage partner fares to earn MQDs quickly. This is because these flights earn MQDs based on a percentage of the flight distance rather than the ticket price.

If you go this route, know that earning rates vary depending on which carrier and fare class you fly. For example, an Air France flight in full economy will earn MQDs based on 20% of the miles flown, while a full economy WestJet ticket will earn 15% of the miles flown. Remember, MQDs are not to be confused with SkyMiles.

You can also earn 1 MQD per dollar spent on Delta Vacations, the airline's platform for booking all-in-one vacation packages. However, Delta Car Rentals and Delta Stays bookings no longer earn MQDs.

Some Delta cobranded credit cards allow cardholders to earn MQDs. The following cards give you an automatic 2,500 MQDs each year (known as MQD Headstart), plus additional MQDs when you spend on the card:

It may be worth applying for one of these cards to close the gap for next year's Medallion status. If you already have one and your everyday purchases won't get you close enough to your desired status level, you might consider ways to increase your spending temporarily — such as paying your rent or mortgage with your cobranded card or making purchases for a friend and having them pay you back.

Just be aware that purchases on these cards must post to your account in 2026 to help you qualify for elite status in the 2027 status year. Purchases made in late December may go toward the following year instead, depending on the transaction date submitted to American Express by the merchant (which may differ from the date when you made the purchase). For example, if you make a purchase on Dec. 31 and the merchant lists the transaction date as Jan. 1, the MQDs you earn will count toward next year instead of this year.

Related: Delta SkyMiles Reserve Amex card review

Delta SkyMiles has historically been one of the most generous programs when it comes to status challenges. After temporary unavailability during recent program changes, the SkyMiles Medallion Status Match Challenge has returned. This means travelers who hold elite status with another airline can request a match through Delta Medallion. If approved, you'll receive the equivalent Delta status for three months, along with a status challenge to extend your shiny new Medallion status.

In 2025, Delta also offered a new program called Elevate Your Status that allowed members to make a one-time MQD purchase to reach the next Medallion status tier, as long as they already had the required number of MQDs to qualify. This limited-time promotion has ended, but keep an eye out in case Delta brings it back for 2026.

Delta's Choice Benefits for Platinum and Diamond members include MQD Accelerators to help you get closer to next year's status. In 2026, Platinum members can select this Choice Benefit to boost their MQDs by 1,000, while Diamond members can earn an extra 2,000 MQDs this way. These MQDs typically take six to eight weeks to deposit into your account — so, if you plan to use this route to achieve next year's status, now is the time to make your Choice Benefit selection.

Another Choice Benefit option allows you to gift Medallion status to other members. Platinum Medallions can choose to gift Silver Medallion status to four people, and Diamonds can gift Gold status to four people. So be nice to friends or family who might be able to give you a hand up into the club.

Note that Platinum status members can select one Choice Benefit, and Diamond status members can select three benefits. You can select your Choice Benefit as soon as you earn status, and you have until Jan. 31, 2027, to select your 2026 benefits.

Related: The ultimate guide to Delta Choice Benefits

This option is probably not feasible for most travelers, but it's worth mentioning.

Thanks to Delta's partnership with Wheels Up, a private jet subscription service, Wheels Up members can receive one Diamond Medallion status for every $100,000 spent in a Wheels Up Fund during a calendar year. If you don't have a subscription, you can still get one Diamond Medallion status after making at least $125,000 in flight spend. However, travelers who earn status either way will not get access to Choice Benefits.

This is obviously not the cheapest option for earning Delta elite status. However, if you or your business use the service anyway, it may be a good way to bypass the other requirements and go straight to the top.

Even though 2026 is coming to a close, there's still time to level up your Delta Medallion elite status so you can travel in comfort next year.

The most important thing is to know where you stand after accounting for the rest of your planned travel for this year. Once you determine how many extra MQDs you need, you can use these strategies to ensure you earn your desired elite tier for next year — and all the perks that come with it.

#6143. Transfer Citi ThankYou Points To Turkish Miles&Smiles With 40% Bonus: Worth It?

At the moment, it’s possible to earn up to a 40% bonus when you transfer Citi ThankYou points to Turkish Airlines Miles&Smiles. However, the bonus isn’t being offered on Citi’s end, but instead, is being offered on Turkish Airlines’ end.

Between November 1 and November 30, 2026, it’s possible to receive a 40% bonus when you move points from the Citi ThankYou program in the United States to Turkish Airlines Miles&Smiles. However, there are some important terms to be aware of:

Ordinarily points transfer at a 1:1 ratio (in 1,000 point increments), while through this promotion you’d get 1,400 Miles&Smiles miles for every 1,000 Citi ThankYou points transferred, though only after the fact.

There are several great cards earning Citi ThankYou points, including the Citi Strata Premier® Card (learn more) and Citi Strata Elite℠ Card (learn more), and it’s easy to combine points between the cards.

Back in the day, the Turkish Airlines Miles&Smiles program offered incredible redemption values across the board, but that’s no longer really the case. At this point, I’d say the sweet spot with the Miles&Smiles program is if you’re looking to travel on Turkish Airlines specifically to or from Istanbul.

That’s because the Miles&Smiles program now charges per segment for awards on Turkish Airlines metal. You can find the cost of one-way saver awards below, just to give you a sense of pricing.

So as an example, a one-way business class award between the United States and Istanbul will cost you 65,000 miles. In other words, with a 40% transfer bonus, you’d be paying around 47,000 Citi ThankYou points for a business class award, which is a pretty great deal.

If you know what you’re doing and have specific redemption plans in mind, this could be a great deal. Just be sure you understand the complexities of the program, and read my guide to the Turkish Miles&Smiles program. Also keep in mind the Miles&Smiles expiration policy, which is that miles expire at the end of the third year after which they’re earned, regardless of activity.

The other big restriction is that the bonus miles will only post after the campaign is done, so you couldn’t transfer points and then immediately redeem all of them (including the bonus). The cap on 50,000 bonus miles is also limiting. But hey, if you value Turkish miles, this could definitely offer some value.

If you’re looking to travel on Turkish Airlines to or from Istanbul, there are some good deals to be had by taking advantage of this.

#6142. Thailand’s 2032 Tourism Plan Chases Spending, Not Arrivals

Enter your email for a complimentary article + exclusive offers.

Photo Credit: Thailand tourism Pixabay / remideligeon

Thailand’s $118 billion goal targets spending rather than arrivals, which have stalled at about 33 million. Rising prices will surely lift revenue regardless, but higher rates aren’t the same as higher value, and the plan has no budget yet for the terminals, marinas and guides needed to attract bigger spenders.

Thailand is targeting at least 4 trillion baht ($118 billion) in annual tourism revenue by 2032 under a draft five-year national plan. That’s about 48% more than the 2.7 trillion baht it earned in 2025, including domestic tourism. The plan also aims to lift Thailand into the top 30 of the World Economic Forum's Travel & Tourism Development Index.

The targets come as Thailand's foreign arrivals are poised to fall for a second straight year.

The Fourth National Tourism Development Plan focuses on raising the economic value of tourism, lifting service standards, winning higher-spending visitors, and spreading income to small businesses and communities.

Cruise and yacht tourism are high-revenue segments where Thailand lacks capacity, the government said. “The country still needs more cruise terminals and yacht marinas to meet demand,” it noted, and asked the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) to draw up an infrastructure framework with other age

Thailand has set a target of at least 4 trillion baht ($118 billion) in annual tourism revenue by 2032 under a draft Fourth National Tourism Development Plan, about 48% above the 2.7 trillion baht earned in 2025. The target requires roughly 5.8% annual growth at a time when arrivals are heading for a second consecutive down year: foreign arrivals fell 7.2% to 32.9 million in 2025, were down 4.1% through October 17, and the government has cut its 2026 forecast to 33 million from 36.7 million. With volume stalled, the plan leans on spending per visitor through cruise and yacht tourism, higher-spending source markets, events, and dispersal beyond Bangkok and the beaches, plus entry-rule changes including a 450-baht ($13) tourist fee targeted for the first quarter of 2027, faster e-visa processing, and shorter immigration waits at Suvarnabhumi. The government named Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Singapore as priority short-haul markets, leaving out China, still Thailand's largest source market this year but down to 4.4 million visitors in 2025 from 11 million in 2019. Analysts quoted said the revenue target is easier to hit than an arrivals target in an inflationary period, but the plan names no budget, no arrivals assumption, and no spending-per-visitor goal, and the cruise terminals and marinas it calls for have no funding or timeline.

#6141. British Airways Flight Attendant Hands Passenger Paper Towels And A Spray Bottle For Urine-Soaked Seat On 8-Hour Flight

A British Airways passenger says she boarded an eight hour flight from Miami to London Heathrow, sat down, and discovered her seat was soaked in urine. Her pants were wet, and she says a flight attendant told her there were no empty seats and she could have paper towels and a tiny bottle of antibacterial cleaning spray to deal with the mess – she couldn’t even have an extra blanket. The passenger shared the story on November 1 and posted the video the following day. Her tweet has been viewed more than 1.6 million times. .@British_Airways ABSOLUTELY disgusted. Boarded my flight from MIA to LHR and my seat for my 8 hour flight is urine-soaked. you could smell it before you even got to my seat and the staff said there is nothing they can do, not even any extra blankets, only a tiny hand sanitiser https://t.co/87NczAMOFj — sof⁷🐺 ⊙⊝⊜ LONDON SOUNDCHECK (@witchiminie) November 1, 2026 The bottle in her photo is labeled 15ml Antibacterial Cleaning Spray. She says she asked for something to put on the seat and was told there were no spare blankets. So she layered paper towels, her own bag, and her blanket over it. @libraryofsofia Watch her account of the British Airways seat incident She first thought someone was cooking fish nearby. Then she worried the passengers around her would think she wet herself. British Airways Sent Her To A Complaint Form British Airways first replied five hours and 23 minutes after her tweet. They apologized and said, “If you’d like to make a formal complaint,” go to the website. The following day, another rep asked her to send her booking details and follow the chat menu to reach an agent. They wanted this off social media! A passenger may have had an accident on the previous flight. The time between flights is the opportunity to switch cushions. And if it’s noticed by the passenger on the ground, as much as other passengers might not want to take a delay, it’s still possible to make the switch especially since there were no other seats available. I’ve argued before that a seat which can’t be properly cleaned should be treated as out of service. Having sold every other seat doesn’t make this one usable. Either fix the seat or it’s an involuntary denied boarding with cash compensation. British Airways Has Done This Before In 2017, I wrote about a British Airways passenger flying London to Cape Town who found his seat soaked in urine. He said a flight attendant handed him wipes to clean it himself. He covered it with a plastic bag and a blanket for the 11-and-a-half-hour flight. BA initially offered him 5,000 Avios. That became a £435 voucher or an upgrade on his next Cape Town flight after he complained. In 2018, a British Airways business class passenger headed to Jamaica found his pillow, seat and trousers wet with urine. He was moved away from his wife and offered 40,000 Avios. Last year, I also covered a Boston – London Heathrow passenger’s story of a woman urinating in her premium economy seat. #6140. Is the Venture X Business worth the $395 annual fee?

The Capital One Venture X Business is a great option for small-business owners who want to earn miles on their spending. It features a solid welcome bonus and many of our favorite features found on its consumer counterpart, the Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card.

One such similarity is the $395 annual fee. This is a bargain compared to some other premium business cards, such as The Business Platinum Card® from American Express with its $895 fee (see rates and fees).

Still, a $395 annual fee is a meaningful expense. Does the Venture X Business offer enough benefits and earning potential to justify that premium fee? Here's what you need to know if you're on the fence.

Currently, new Venture X Business applicants can earn up to 300,000 bonus miles and a $1,000 travel credit:

*To use within 16 months from account opening

This bonus is worth up to $6,550 when you factor in TPG's November valuations of Capital One miles at 1.85 cents and the travel credit.

If you can meet the steep minimum spending requirements, the bonus alone is valuable enough to justify paying the card's $395 annual fee more than 16 times over.

Related: How to maximize your Capital One miles

Beyond the Venture X Business welcome bonus, you'll earn:

And when it comes to redeeming your miles, you have options. If you want to keep it simple, you can redeem your miles for a statement credit to cover travel expenses (charged to the card within the previous 90 days). This option offers a value of 1 cent per mile.

To get more value out of your miles, you can also transfer your miles to any of Capital One's 15-plus hotel and airline partners, including valuable options like Air Canada Aeroplan, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer and Wyndham Rewards.

TPG values Capital One miles at 1.85 cents each when used with transfer partners, though the value you receive depends on your redemption.

This makes the Venture X Business an especially attractive option for big-spending business owners who don't want to worry about bonus categories.

With this card, you can feel confident knowing you're earning valuable rewards no matter what you're buying.

Related: Should you transfer Capital One miles to partners or redeem them directly?

Venture X Business cardholders receive $300 in credits each year for travel booked through Capital One Business Travel. This credit is automatic, making it relatively easy to use.

However, since the credit is limited to travel booked through Capital One Business Travel, you'll likely give up any hotel or rental car elite status perks. The drawbacks of booking through a portal can put a damper on the value of this annual credit.

Still, fully taking advantage of this perk will bring your effective annual fee down to just $95.

Related: How to decide whether to book travel directly or through a portal

The travel credit isn't the only annual perk you'll get as a Venture X Business cardholder. Every year, on your account anniversary, you'll also receive 10,000 bonus miles, worth $185 according to our valuations.

Even if you redeem these anniversary miles directly for travel at a rate of 1 cent per mile, this annual bonus is worth $100. This perk and the travel credit combined more than justify the card's $395 annual fee each year.

As a Venture X Business primary cardholder, you get unlimited access to Capital One Lounges, currently open at:

Capital One also operates dining-focused "Landing" facilities at LaGuardia Airport (LGA) and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA).

This card also includes access to Priority Pass lounges.

Without an eligible credit card, you can pay $90 for a lounge day pass. Five visits alone would cost $450 out of pocket, so you'll make up the annual fee's value quickly if you can take advantage of your Capital One Lounge access.

Related: Capital One Venture X vs. Venture X Business

On top of these benefits, the Venture X Business includes additional travel perks:

These benefits are more difficult to quantify, but they'll provide added comfort and peace of mind during your travels.

Related: A comparison of luxury hotel programs from credit card issuers: Amex, Capital One, Chase and Citi

If you can take advantage of key Venture X Business benefits, such as the annual travel credit and anniversary bonus miles, you can offset the card's annual fee year after year.

However, if you can't maximize the annual travel credit or airport lounge access, you may want to go with another of our favorite business credit cards. You may also want to consider a different card if you anticipate struggling to meet this card's lofty welcome bonus spending requirements.

For more details, read our full review of the Venture X Business.

#6139. Former China Eastern Chairman Jailed In $10+ Million Bribery Scandal

The former chairman of China Eastern Airlines has been sentenced to 14 years in jail, as he accepted more than $10 million in bribes in his official role. Yowzers!

A court in China’s Liaoning Province has sentenced former China Eastern chairman Liu Shaoyong to prison. The court ruled that he accepted over $10 million in bribes in his official capacity as chairman of one of China’s largest airlines.

The court found that between 2002 and 2023, Liu abused his position at the airline to provide assistance to companies and individuals in business operations, project contracts, and flight route management. Liu has been sentenced to 14 years in prison, and has been ordered to pay a fine of $600K, plus his illicit gains and related proceeds have to be recovered.

While the court ruled that his conduct constituted bribery “in an exceedingly large amount,” the sentence he got was actually lighter than it could’ve been, due to mitigating circumstances. These include his confession, voluntary disclosure of previously unknown offenses, and expression of remorse and cooperation in recovering illicit gains.

Make of this what you will, but it’s interesting to note that this is all part of China’s “anti-corruption campaign,” targeting officials at various levels, including executives of state-owned enterprises.

In June 2025, Liu had been placed under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) and the National Commission of Supervision, for violations of party discipline and state laws. In January 2026, he was expelled from the Communist Party of China (CPC), after investigators found that he had abused his authority for personal gain, and he was formally charged in May 2026.

China Eastern’s former chairman has been sentenced to 14 years in prison, after he admitted to taking over $10 million in bribes in his official role. This came as part of a larger crackdown by the government, which also saw the executive expelled from the Communist Party of China.

Over the years we’ve seen a decent number of airline executives charged with corruption — after all, they control a lot of spending, and in some cases, might get influenced for the wrong reasons.

What do you make of this punishment for China Eastern’s former chairman?

Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam said the airline wants to add more widebody aircraft to its order book, even as the group posted consolidated losses of more than INR 220 billion ($2.3 billion) in fiscal 2026 — more than double the prior year. Speaking at the Aviation India and South Asia 2026 conference in New Delhi, Gebremariam said Air India has 600 aircraft on firm order, of which 80 are widebodies, and is in discussions with Airbus and Boeing about more. The airline is also rethinking its hubs: Pakistani airspace closure has hit Delhi harder than Mumbai, so more Europe and North America flying moves to Mumbai, Delhi grows eastward, and Bengaluru is under consideration as a third hub. Costs are the immediate problem. "Our cost is greater than our revenue," Gebremariam said, and a cross-functional team is looking for savings and shared corporate functions with Air India Express. He gave no timeframe for a return to profitability. The growth target is clear: win back third- and fourth-freedom India-international traffic currently flown by foreign carriers, grow international-to-international connections from about 10% of the business, and push the full-service Air India brand further upmarket while Air India Express holds the low-cost segment.

#6137. Ill-Fated Learjet Had Altitude Struggles Amid Severe Turbulence 6 Months Ago, ATC Audio Shows

The Learjet 60 that crashed in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people onboard, had experienced a troubling encounter with severe turbulence just six months earlier. Resurfaced air traffic control audio from May 2026 reveals that the same aircraft struggled to maintain its assigned altitude near Newark, New Jersey, prompting a controller to challenge the crew's description of the conditions as merely moderate turbulence.

The revelation, originally reported by the Daily Express, raises questions about similarities between the two incidents, particularly in how the pilots characterized the turbulence they encountered. Before Sunday's fatal crash, the Learjet's crew also reported moderate turbulence despite altitude fluctuations of up to 700 feet. However, investigators have not established a connection between the incidents, and the identities of the pilots involved in the May incident remain unconfirmed.

The earlier encounter occurred in May, when the Learjet, registered as N722BD, was flying near Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR). According to audio obtained by The US Sun, a controller noticed the business jet climbing unexpectedly and questioned the crew. A female pilot responded that they were "just about to call you," said they were experiencing moderate turbulence, and were unable to maintain their assigned altitude.

The controller immediately challenged that assessment and instructed the pilots to descend to 4,000 feet. The situation was particularly concerning because another business jet was operating nearby at a similar altitude, potentially creating a separation issue. A male pilot subsequently reiterated that the Learjet was experiencing moderate chop, but the controller insisted that an inability to maintain altitude indicated more serious conditions.

"If you can't maintain altitude, that's not moderate. That's severe turbulence."

The controller then explicitly asked whether the aircraft was encountering severe turbulence, prompting affirmative responses from both pilots. When questioned about possible injuries, the female pilot reported none, but confirmed that severe turbulence was continuing. The identities of the two pilots have not been established, and there is no confirmation that either was aboard the aircraft during its fatal flight six months later.

The May exchange highlights an important distinction in how pilots report turbulence. Under the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) turbulence classifications, moderate turbulence can produce changes in altitude, attitude, and airspeed, but pilots should retain positive control. Severe turbulence involves larger, more abrupt changes and can leave an aircraft momentarily out of position. The controller's concern was therefore consistent with established aviation terminology.

Slight, irregular changes in altitude or attitude

Changes in altitude or attitude, with positive control maintained

Large, abrupt changes; aircraft may be momentarily out of position

Aircraft violently tossed about; control practically impossible

This distinction matters in congested airspace, where aircraft must maintain assigned altitudes to preserve separation from other traffic. An unexpected climb or descent can create a potential conflict even when the deviation is caused by atmospheric conditions rather than pilot action. Accurate turbulence reports also help controllers warn following aircraft and coordinate alternative altitudes. However, difficulty maintaining altitude does not automatically establish a mechanical problem or loss of control.

For N722BD, the May recording indicates that the aircraft deviated up to 700 feet above and 400 feet below its assigned altitude of 4,000 feet. That suggests that the initial description of a "moderate chop" significantly understated the difficulties the crew was experiencing, and supports the controller's assessment of severe turbulence.

This article serves as reassurance that turbulence rarely poses a danger to passengers and requires little effort from pilots to navigate.

N722BD departed Austin Bergstrom International Airport (AUS), bound for North Eleuthera Airport (ELH) in the Bahamas, carrying seven passengers and two pilots. While crossing South Florida at 35,000 feet, the crew reported light clear icing and turbulence, with altitude deviations of approximately 600-700 feet. The similarities to May are striking: once again, pilots aboard the same aircraft described "moderate turbulence" while experiencing substantial altitude fluctuations. Nevertheless, those fluctuations alone do not prove that the November conditions met the FAA's severe classification.

After encountering precipitation, the crew requested permission to climb to 37,000 feet, hoping to find smoother conditions. ATC approved the request, but less than 30 seconds later, the pilots reported an uncontrolled descent and declared an emergency. According to Flightradar24, the aircraft's reported descent rate exceeded 32,000 feet per minute before it crashed in Palm Beach County, killing everyone aboard.

The NTSB investigation has already uncovered evidence of an inflight breakup, including pieces of the aircraft's left elevator found between 1.3 miles (2.1 km) and 3.8 miles (6.1 km) from the impact site. Investigators are examining weather, aircraft systems, maintenance records, and flight communications. Although both encounters involved turbulence and difficulties maintaining altitude, no causal connection has been established. A preliminary report is expected within about 30 days, and the final investigation will likely take considerably longer.

#6136. $12,000 Buffalo–New York Fares Making Headlines—I’m Finding Nonstops For $337 Roundtrip

A $12,203 airfare between Buffalo and New York about 300 miles each way – is going viral as evidence of how expensive it’s gotten to fly home for the holidays. The TikTok video that started it off though shows a roundtrip price (not one-way) and connecting both directions in Florida (not non-stop). Meanwhile, nonstops on that route seem to start at $337 roundtrip. Kristen Mirand says she was trying to get home to Buffalo and received a notification for a $200 flight from New York. Then she looked at returning, and found five-figure prices with connections in Orlando and Fort Lauderdale. She joked that she’d start walking. The New York Post ran with “Flight from Buffalo to NYC reportedly reached $12K — as holiday airfare hits an all-time high” and suggests higher fuel costs and holiday demand are involved here. ZeroHedge describes a “roughly 90 minute flight,” and launches into airlines keeping fares high after fuel prices fall. It ends with the prospect of airlines “laughing all the way to the bank.” Look at the flights actually displayed in the video: $11,400 roundtrip, returning through Orlando. These are 7 and 9 hour trips from Buffalo to JFK. $12,203 roundtrip, returning through Fort Lauderdale. These are 7 and 8.5 hour trips. Every price is labeled round trip. you’re seeing the cost of the whole ticket when you select a return. This wasn’t a $12,000 nonstop and none of these itineraries gets you there in 90 minutes. I’m seeing nonstop roundtrips around $337 on Delta Air Lines, JetBlue, United Airlines and American Airlines, checking across the New York airports. Even if you want to connect in Florida, Frontier Airlines can be as low as $210 roundtrip. She doesn’t show her dates, but at those prices be flexible! My guess is that the pricing is breaking somewhere as the system puts together this unnatural itinerary. A fare between Buffalo and New York comes with rules about how you can travel and Florida connections aren’t usually included in the routing rules. A search can wind up combining separate fares for different pieces of the trip instead of using the simple fare between the two cities. Bad fare combining or an error putting together the outbound and return can cause weird outcomes. While the last seats on a flight can be expensive, “last seat available” doesn’t seem like the explanation for a $12,000 Buffalo–New York price. Airfares are up. Hopper’s says Thanksgiving domestic roundtrips average $402, up 31%, and Christmas $452, up 23%. With millions of fare quotes being generated, even a tiny error rate is going to produce outlier results. Mistake fares can be fares that are too high, not just too low. Faced with a fare like this, I’d: Search for nonstops on the date I actually want. Start with the trip I’d choose to take before considering a seven-hour detour. Check JFK, LaGuardia and Newark. Restricting the search to one airport leaves out alternatives that may work just as well. Search the airline websites directly. See whether the airline produces the same price, rather than treating one Google Flights result as the answer. Start a fresh search and compare one-ways with the roundtrip. Check the dates, cabin, passenger count and currency. Separate searches can get you away from whatever combination generated the nonsense price. For this route I’d also price Amtrak’s Empire Service between Buffalo and New York. Those Florida connections already consume most of the day before you add getting to the airport, security and the trip into Manhattan. Airport lounges can serve as oases from a busy, crowded or outdated terminal. Some lounges participate in membership networks like Priority Pass, while others, like the United Club lounge, are operated by individual airlines.

If you’re a loyal United Airlines flyer or frequent one of the carrier’s largest hubs, visiting a United Club lounge is probably already on your radar. However, the airline made some major access changes in 2025.

Here's what you need to know about accessing United's lounges.

The Chicago-based airline operates a network of standard lounges known as United Clubs, as well as more exclusive Polaris lounges for eligible premium-cabin travelers on select long-haul international, transcontinental and Hawaii routes. Both offer complimentary food, drinks and Wi-Fi, while Polaris lounges feature additional amenities, such as sit-down dining, relaxation areas and shower suites.

So, how can travelers gain access to United's network of lounges?

You'll need a same-day boarding pass to access United lounges. This can be a same-day boarding pass for a United-operated flight or a flight operated by a Star Alliance partner airline, like Lufthansa or Swiss.

Related: Best United Airlines credit cards

United now has two tiers of paid membership for entry to the Club.

This membership offers the primary member unlimited access to all 45-plus United Club locations. There are no discounts available for United Premier members. Individual members can pay to bring guests into the lounge on a one-off basis; a one-time pass costs $59 per guest and is subject to availability.

Individual members do not have access to Star Alliance partner lounges.

Annual fee: Varies depending on Premier status

All Access members can enjoy unlimited United Club access for the primary member and up to two adult guests, or one adult and any dependents under 18.

This membership also includes access to Star Alliance partner lounges and other select partner locations, subject to applicable access policies.

Lifetime United Club members have been converted to All Access memberships.

TPG values United MileagePlus miles at 1.2 cents each per our November 2026 valuations, so your best bet is to pay the annual membership fee with cash rather than miles.

Having an eligible cobranded United credit card can be the most cost-effective way to consistently enter the United Club.

You can get lounge access with the following cards (note that some cards only offer one-time passes):

*The information for the United Club Business Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Unlike a paid Individual membership, a United Club membership earned via a cobranded credit card offers a unique access policy that includes entry for primary cardmembers, one adult guest and any dependents under 18 years old.

Cardmembers can unlock an All Access membership, which increases the guest allowance and provides access to participating Star Alliance partner lounges, by earning Premier Gold status or higher, or by spending $50,000 on eligible purchases with their United Club Card or United Club Business Card in a calendar year.

Since the annual fee on both the United Club Card and the United Club Business Card is $695, having a credit card to enter the lounge remains a more attractive option than outright buying a membership.

Additionally, the United Club Card and the United Club Business Card offer four one-time passes on each account anniversary. A pass can be used by one person accompanying the primary cardholder or an authorized user into the lounge.

If you’d prefer to avoid the hefty annual fee, you can opt for the entry-level United Explorer Card or the United Business Card, both of which include two single-use United Club passes each year. Note that these day passes don’t include guest access, nor can they be transferred to friends or family who aren't authorized users or accompanying a cardmember into the lounge.

Certain MileagePlus Premier and Star Alliance Gold members can access United Clubs when traveling on eligible flights.

United Premier Gold (and higher) members can access United Clubs when traveling internationally on United or another Star Alliance carrier, regardless of their class of service. They can also bring along one guest who's traveling on the same flight.

Travelers who earn Star Alliance Gold status through another member airline can access United Clubs when flying on any eligible Star Alliance flight, including domestic United flights. Again, guests must be traveling on the same flight as the elite member.

United’s invite-only Global Services members can enjoy lounge access on all United-operated flights, including those operating exclusively within the U.S. Note that this new perk only covers the Global Services member — you’ll only be able to bring a guest into the lounge with an All Access membership, eligible cobranded credit card or when flying internationally.

Travelers flying in certain premium cabins on United or its Star Alliance partners can also access United Clubs. However, eligibility and guest privileges vary by airline, route and cabin class, as outlined below.

If you don’t travel enough to justify an annual membership, you can also purchase a one-time United Club pass for $59 per person at United Club locations or through the United mobile app. Just note that day passes don’t guarantee entry when lounge is at capacity.

Travelers using a one-time pass can enter a United Club only up to three hours before their scheduled departure time. (This exclusively applies to departure flights, and there is no time limit for entry on connecting flights.) These one-time passes are not accepted at grab-and-go locations, United Polaris lounges, United Arrivals Lounges or partner lounges.

You can also earn complimentary one-time passes with select cobranded credit cards, including:

One-time passes issued through United cobranded credit cards must be redeemed by the primary cardholder, an authorized user or a guest accompanied by either. Each pass admits one person.

United’s lounges are open to a few other travelers, including:

Some premium-class passengers also have access to United’s Polaris lounges, which offer a more premium experience. You can expect modern furnishings, private spa-like shower suites and elevated culinary options.

Three types of passengers are eligible for Polaris lounge access:

In addition to United Clubs and Polaris Lounges, the carrier operates a grab-and-go lounge concept called United Club Fly.

The first such space opened at Denver International Airport (DEN) in November 2022, and a second one opened at George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) in 2025. Eligible travelers can enter Club Fly by scanning their boarding pass at the self-service entry gate.

Once inside, you can head to the snack bar that’s stocked with packaged and prepared foods. You can also order a coffee from the barista.

Given Club Fly’s focus on efficiency, the access policies are a bit different. Eligible United Club members and travelers flying in international premium cabins are eligible to enter, but they cannot bring any guests.

The Chicago-based carrier operates more than 45 United Club lounge locations. Of course, you’ll find a plethora of United Clubs in the carrier’s main hubs, including:

Apart from DEN, all of the aforementioned airports also have Polaris lounges.

There are other United Club locations scattered across the U.S., including in airports such as Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), Philadelphia International Airport (PHL), Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX), Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) and Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport (MSP), among others.

Check out United's website for a complete list of the airline's Club and Polaris lounge locations.

United offers a variety of ways to access its United Clubs, both for premium-cabin frequent flyers and for those with a membership.

If you frequently travel with United, it’s worth analyzing which options offer the best bang for your buck to unlock a relaxing lounge experience.

#6134. Air Serbia Flight To Moscow Diverts After Politician Reportedly Skips Security

An Air Serbia flight that was supposed to fly from Serbia to Russia ended up turning around over Lithuania, in order for additional security checks to be carried out on passengers. The circumstances surrounding this sure are unusual, given who was onboard.

This incident happened on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and involves Air Serbia flight JU134, scheduled to fly from Belgrade (BEG) to Moscow (SVO). The 1,074-mile flight was operated by an Airbus A320 with the registration code YU-APH. The flight was scheduled to depart at 6:25PM and land at 11:40PM, with a two hour time change, so it was blocked at 3hr15min.

The plane took off at 6:48PM, basically on schedule, and it started flying north, over Hungary, Slovakia, Poland, and then Lithuania. However, around 90 minutes after takeoff, while more than halfway, the plane u-turned, and flew back toward Belgrade.

The plane ended up landing in Belgrade at 9:57PM local time, a little over three hours after it first departed. The plane ended up once again taking off in the early morning hours of November 4, departing at 1:56AM, and landing at 6:43AM, over seven hours behind schedule.

Diversions happen, though it’s definitely unusual for a flight to turn around to the origin when it’s already more than halfway to its destination, especially when maintenance wasn’t to blame. Officially, the airline has shared that the decision to divert was made “in accordance with the instructions received and all applicable security rules.” That’s obviously really vague, though… so what really happened?

Here’s where the story gets really interesting. Onboard this Air Serbia flight were a few associates of former Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic, who just recently lost an election. One of the people onboard was Aleksandar Vulin, who served as deputy prime minister until 2025, and is viewed as being very pro-Russia. The US had even imposed sanctions on him due to his close ties with Russia.

Media reports in Serbia suggest that the reason for the diversion was that security camera footage at Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport had been reviewed, and it was determined that someone had helped him avoid security checks. Now, I understand the need to carry out security checks, though I’m also not sure the point of diverting when you’re already more than halfway to your destination.

Vulin denies that he was the reason that the plane diverted, claiming that it was instead a political showdown. After the diversion, he went on national TV in Serbia, to say the following:

“It’s all a lie, an act of violence and an attempt to prove to these new authorities how ready they are here at the airport, how much they are on the defensive of their ideology. So, of course it’s all a lie, of course it’s all utter nonsense. I’m really sorry and uncomfortable, so many people have returned, their lives are being ruined, their obligations are being ruined because of the attempt to politically deal with me.”

“I am completely calm, I know that I am in the right. And you know, I did not go to Moscow as a tourist, I went on business. I am going there to fight for the extension of the gas agreement. Not for me and you, but for all citizens of Serbia.”

He also said he was asleep at the time of the diversion, and had no clue what was going on until the plane landed back in Belgrade:

“We just woke up, to be honest, I fell asleep. I was sleeping on the plane, I wake up, they say: You are in Belgrade. How are you in Belgrade? When we went outside, I see the police, the special forces gathered. I say: ‘Colleagues, have you come for me?’ They laugh. They say: ‘We are not, Minister.’ I go down with all the other passengers. I go through the procedure with all the other passengers again. I go through another procedure by myself. And now, I am standing and waiting for them to let us get on the plane again.”

An Air Serbia flight from Belgrade to Moscow turned around while over halfway to its destination. The decision to divert was made in accordance with “applicable security rules,” and all passengers were screened when the plane landed back in Serbia.

While it’s believed that a pro-Russia Serbian politician who was onboard may have avoided security checks at the airport, the politician denies that, and claims this was a political move.

What do you make of this unusual Air Serbia diversion?

A Delta Air Lines passenger shouted “I love myself!” while two Port Authority police officers struggled to get him off a plane at New York JFK. And he wanted everyone onboard to know how strong he was. This man used racial slurs and encouraged people to post his removal on Instagram. I shared that last month but now there’s brand new footage. Watch the additional passenger video shared by TMZ The incident happened October 22 aboard Delta flight 2342 from New York JFK to Atlanta. The aircraft was still at the gate. Port Authority police say the Brooklyn man appeared to be intoxicated. The original recording shows him being escorted through the cabin, swearing and using racial slurs. He looks toward the people filming and calls out, “Put it on Instagram!” He’d reportedly been making threats, shouting “death to America,” and making gun noises. Delta apologized to passengers, thanked police, and reiterated its “zero tolerance for disruptive behavior.” Federal rules prohibit boarding someone who appears intoxicated. #6132. Regional Visitors Keep Oman’s Arrivals Steady but Can’t Fill Its Hotels

Photo Caption: Traditional dhow boat in Muscat, Oman.

Oman’s arrivals have held up this year, but its hotels lost more than a tenth of their guests and revenue as Europeans stayed away. Regional travelers are still arriving but make shorter visits at lower rates.

Oman’s hotels are taking a far bigger hit from the U.S.-Iran war than the country’s headline arrival numbers suggest, Skift’s analysis of tourism data shows.

The country received 2.5 million visitors from January to August, down 0.8% year over year, according to the National Centre for Statistics and Information’s (NCSI) latest tourism report. The figures are the most recent available official arrivals data. In 2025, the country drew nearly 4 million visitors, against a Vision 2040 long-term target of 11 million a year.

Over the first eight months of this year, guest numbers at Oman’s three- to five-star hotels fell 10.7% to 1.35 million, shrinking hotel revenue by 11% to 156.5 million Omani rials ($407 million).

The most recent data shows no recovery. September occupancy at Oman hotels fell 6.4 percentage points year over year to 47.3% from 53.7%, according to CoStar. Average daily rate dr

Oman's headline visitor numbers look almost flat, but its hotels are absorbing a much deeper hit from the U.S.-Iran war and wider regional conflict. Total arrivals fell 0.8% to 2.5 million between January and August, while guests at three- to five-star hotels dropped 10.7% to 1.35 million and hotel revenue fell 11% to $407 million, according to the National Centre for Statistics and Information. International air passengers fell 9.7% on 9.1% fewer flights, while domestic passengers rose 5.2%, suggesting land crossings from the UAE and Yemen are propping up the headline figure. September data from CoStar shows no recovery: occupancy fell 6.4 points to 47.3%, average daily rate dropped 10.5% to about $100, and RevPAR fell 21% to about $47. Hotel guest mix data points to European losses as a driver, and Gulf Hotels warned in a Muscat Stock Exchange filing that 2026 revenue and profit could fall short of budget, with its chairman citing the continued conflict in the Gulf region and connectivity problems to key European source markets. Operators describe shorter stays, later bookings, and heavy reliance on regional and local demand. Supply is slipping too, with Oman now set to add 700 rooms by year-end rather than the previously forecast total, and 3,100 more rooms due across 2027 and 2028.

#6131. Is World Of Hyatt Points + Cash Worth It? The Value Varies Wildly

While the most popular way to redeem World of Hyatt points is for free night redemptions, the program also has a Points + Cash option, whereby you can redeem part points and part cash toward the cost of a hotel stay.

The reality is that the value of Hyatt Points + Cash has fluctuated significantly over the years. Going back a decade, it was the primary way that I redeemed my points. Then it was devalued significantly, and then some value was brought back. So I’d like to take a look at the current state of things… is Hyatt Points + Cash worth considering nowadays?

As the name suggests, with Hyatt Points + Cash, you can redeem part points and part cash toward the cost of a Hyatt stay. More specifically, you’ll redeem 50% of the points required for a stay, and will receive a 30-50% discount off the standard rate for the room type chosen.

Now, there are some important things to be aware of:

Just as a reminder, below is the standard room World of Hyatt award chart, which shows the award pricing for a free night hotel stay based on which of the five pricing tiers applies for a particular night (lowest, low, moderate, upper, or top).

When booking Points + Cash, you’d pay half of the points, plus 50-70% of the flexible revenue rate, so below is that chart.

With the basics of Hyatt Points + Cash out of the way, let’s do some number crunching. Let me state upfront that based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider World of Hyatt points to be worth 1.4 cents each, though I usually get quite a bit more value out of them in comparison to what a hotel stay would cost with cash.

For the purposes of the below examples, I’ll simply be comparing the cost for a free night redemption to the cost of a Points + Cash redemption. This doesn’t consider the outright cost of a stay if paying cash, so for more on that, see my post about when you should redeem points for a hotel stay.

I picked six hotels at random, belonging to different brands and in different regions. I picked totally random dates, so let’s take a look at what I found.

For the night I picked, the Grand Hyatt Tampa Bay is charging 15,000 points per night, or 7,500 points plus $103 ($116 including taxes & fees). If redeeming outright, you’re spending 7,500 extra points to save $116, which is like buying Hyatt points for 1.55 cents each.

The Park Hyatt Los Cabos is charging 55,000 points per night, or 27,500 points plus $500.50 ($680.68 including taxes & fees). If redeeming outright, you’re spending 27,500 extra points to save $680.68, which is like buying Hyatt points for 2.48 cents each.

The Hyatt Studios Mobile is charging 3,000 points per night, or 1,500 points plus $61 ($71.98 including taxes & fees). If redeeming outright, you’re spending 1,500 extra points to save $71.98, which is like buying Hyatt points for 4.8 cents each.

The Thompson Rome is charging 35,000 points per night, or 17,500 points plus $281.20 (that includes taxes & fees). If redeeming outright, you’re spending 17,500 extra points to save $281.20, which is like buying Hyatt points for 1.61 cents each.

The Hyatt Centric Dubai Jumeirah is charging 20,000 points per night, or 10,000 points plus $115 ($145.14 including taxes & fees). You’re spending $145.14 to save 10,000 points, which is like buying Hyatt points for 1.45 cents each.

The Grand Hyatt Seoul is charging 20,000 points per night, or 10,000 points plus $221 (that includes taxes & fees). You’re spending $221 to save 10,000 points, which is like buying Hyatt points for 2.21 cents each.

As you can see, the value of Hyatt Points + Cash varies significantly. In the above six examples I randomly pulled up, you’re essentially “buying” Hyatt points for anywhere from 1.45 cents to 4.8 cents each (these aren’t actually points in your account, but rather you’re spending some amount of cash in lieu of points).

So the idea is that if the “purchase” price on points were relatively low, it could be worth booking Points + Cash, rather than just redeeming outright. On the low end of the spectrum, some people might find this to be worthwhile, though I think on the high end of the spectrum, we can all agree this represents an awful deal.

Before you make a final decision, just keep in mind:

Lastly, let me just mention that in many cases Points + Cash is a better value compared to redeeming points outright in situations where the cash rate is lower than usual, and a hotel is in low season. In those situations it might not make sense to redeem points at all. This comes down to how reimbursement for these awards works between World of Hyatt and individual hotels.

For example, the single best Points + Cash deal above is at the Hyatt Centric Dubai, but if you look at the cash rate, you’ll see that redeeming points isn’t a great deal in the first place. There’s no reason to redeem 20,000 points (or 10,000 points plus $115) when the cash rate in the first place is well under $200.

Hyatt Points + Cash lets you redeem part points and part cash toward the cost of a hotel stay. While it’s nice to have the flexibility of this redemption opportunity, more often than not it doesn’t represent a good deal, in my opinion.

The value you’re getting per point through Points + Cash does vary wildly, but one thing that’s fairly consistent is that you won’t get outsized value. In a majority of situations where Points + Cash represents a good deal compared to the outright points cost, it’s a hotel where a points redemption isn’t a good deal in the first place.

Personally, I avoid Points + Cash redemptions, though it’s always worth checking and crunching the numbers.

What’s your take on Hyatt’s Points + Cash option? Do you ever use it?

#6130. Baby Moose Wandered Up To Alaska Airlines Check-In Entrance — As One Man Shooes It Away

A baby moose trotted past passengers unloading their bags curbside at Anchorage airport, then stopped near the Alaska Airlines check-in doors. A man simply walked toward it, waved an arm, shooed it away getting it to turn around. The man sharing the video, describes the animal as trying to board an Alaska Airlines flight. If only! It walks past cars and travelers before it pausing near the terminal entrance – door 1 for Air Canada, Alaska Airlines and American. The animal passes close to an open SUV hatch as passengers handle their bags. Another traveler is standing outside the terminal with suitcases when the moose stops nearby. A man approaches from the roadway and the calf heads back along the sidewalk. There’s a potentially sad explanation for why it’s alone. A commenter who says he’s the one that shooed it away reports airport employees told him the calf’s mother had been hit and killed by a vehicle a few days earlier. Anchorage airport regularly reminds travelers about moose around its roads and parking areas. I’ve covered an Alaska Airlines flight delayed by a seal on the runway, polar bears on an Alaska airport taxiway, and a raccoon helping itself to candy at a Philadelphia airport shop. The raccoon at least knew what it wanted. The Amex Platinum Card offers up to $75 in Lululemon statement credits each quarter. If you shop at the retailer only once and spend less than $75, you’ll forfeit any unused portion of the statement credit when the next quarter begins.

To maximize this benefit, first make sure you’re enrolled in the statement credit, then click through a shopping portal before making your purchase. While you’ll earn only 1 point per dollar spent with your Platinum Card, you may be able to pick up additional rewards through a shopping portal. (At the time of publication, Rakuten is not offering rewards on Lululemon purchases.)

Next, aim to use the full $75 statement credit each quarter. You don’t have to spend it all in a single transaction, and you can spread your purchases across multiple orders if needed. Since many popular Lululemon items — including jackets, pants and shirts — cost more than $75, using the entire statement credit shouldn’t be difficult.

If you buy an item you’re not happy with, consider exchanging it instead of returning it. A return could trigger a statement credit reversal, and you may not be able to use your statement credit again during that quarter.

You can also stretch your statement credit further by purchasing sale items. (Note that purchases made at Lululemon outlet locations don’t qualify.)

Finally, don’t wait until the last minute to use your quarterly statement credit. If your purchase doesn’t post before the end of the quarter, it could trigger the following quarter’s statement credit instead.

Don't forget to use your Q4 Lululemon statement credit, since you don't want to leave that value on the table.

#6128. Why Scaling AI Agents Is Harder Than Building Them

Scaling AI agents is less about the model than the systems, talent, and infrastructure around it. As travel companies move from pilots into production, they must decide which capabilities differentiate the business and which are better handled by a specialist.

This sponsored content was created in collaboration with a Skift partner.

AI agents can look remarkably capable in a controlled demo. Putting that same technology in front of real customers, connected to live systems and exposed to unpredictable demand, is another matter.

Skift Research found that 33% of travel operators are experimenting with agentic AI, while just 2% of travel organizations have scaled it. That gap raises a practical question: What changes when an agent moves from a controlled experiment into production?“A demo is designed to show what an agent can do,” said Erik Zahnlecker, travel industry lead at Sierra, a conversational AI platform that helps companies build and deploy AI agents. Sierra works with hotel groups, rental car companies, travel marketplaces, and airlines, including Philippine Airlines. In a demo, the agent typically runs in a controlled environment, without the live systems that affect latency and performance. “Scaling to real production traffic is where you’re testing the agent against real-world environments.”

Moving into production introduces a much wider set of technical requirements. Enterprise AI agents have to connect with existing systems, respond fast enough to sustain a conversation, absorb demand spikes, and follow brand rules at scale. For chief technology and information officers, that turns AI deployment into a broader technology strategy question: What should the company own, and where does a specialized partner make more sense?

The first article in this series explored how AI agents could maintain context across the travel customer lifecycle, connecting service, loyalty, and booking over time. This article looks at the infrastructure required to make that work at scale.

Demos are an important first step in evaluating what an AI agent can do, typically in a controlled environment using mocked data. A proof of concept goes further by testing whether the agent can operate successfully in a limited environment before a company commits to broader deployment. Production then means connecting to real APIs, handling live traffic, and serving customers across what are often millions of conversations a year.

Reaching that stage requires more than technical readiness. Companies also need internal buy-in and a business case for moving forward. Sierra uses proofs of concept to test the technology at a limited production scale and demonstrate return on investment. “We’ve found that there’s no better way than to build together and prove it,” Zahnlecker said.

Deployments then scale in stages. A deployment may begin by handling a narrow set of customer intents and 5% of traffic on a particular channel, then expand incrementally as confidence grows. On the phone, that path can eventually place the agent at the top of the interactive voice response (IVR) menu.

Sierra uses what it calls the “agent iceberg” to illustrate how much of the work required for a production-ready agent sits beyond the model itself. Above the waterline are the parts most teams picture: a large language model (LLM), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), which pulls information from external sources, and tools that allow the agent to interact with other systems.

“We hear this a lot: ‘It’s just an LLM call with some tools and RAG,’” Zahnlecker said. “The reality is companies tend to underestimate what’s under the hood.”

Below the surface are integrations with core systems, the runtime governing how the agent behaves, context management, testing, and optimization. The system has to guard against hallucinations, enforce brand rules, reliably call the right tools, and determine when a task needs a fast model versus one capable of deeper reasoning.

None of that AI agent infrastructure stands still. Zahnlecker said Sierra ships an average of 17 meaningful platform updates a week, and he recalled a recent week when roughly eight new foundational models were released, illustrating the pace an in-house team would have to keep up with just to stay current with the frontier. The question, then, is less whether a large travel company can build an agent than whether maintaining that surrounding stack is where it wants to focus its technical resources.

Three realities are especially pronounced in travel. Each can strain traditional service operations, while also creating a strong use case for AI agents built to handle production conditions.

The first is legacy technology: Some core airline systems have roots in decades-old mainframe infrastructure. AI agents can provide a modern, conversational layer for customers while integrating with those existing systems, but those connections still have to meet conversational latency standards.

The second is volatility. For example, a nor’easter can ground hundreds of flights at once, creating a sudden surge in customer demand. Traditional support teams can struggle to absorb peak volumes, while AI agents built for production can provide additional capacity during demand spikes.

“When 10,000 calls come in at the same moment because hundreds of flights are grounded in the Northeast, traditional support teams can quickly become overwhelmed. AI agents can help absorb that spike because they’re built to scale,” Zahnlecker said.

Those moments also test how the agent responds to customers under stress. Zahnlecker described the goal as handling disruption “with EQ, not just IQ,” combining technical capability with the empathy customers expect when plans go wrong.

The third challenge is language. An international airline may need to serve customers across 20 or more languages and locales, which can be difficult to staff around the clock. Philippine Airlines’ agent, built on Sierra, can switch between Tagalog, Taglish, and English in a single conversation. For global travel brands, that ability can make it easier to serve customers across languages and locales at scale.

Scaling these systems also depends on the people behind them. Data highlighted in Skift Research’s State of Travel 2026 report shows that travel has one of the lowest shares of AI-trained employees among major industries, with just 3% of the industry’s workforce considered AI-trained.

Zahnlecker argues that the relevant question is what kind of AI expertise travel companies need to put the technology to work. Sierra regularly works with in-house data science teams, AI divisions, and product leaders at travel companies, he said. Those teams may not include specialists who pre-train foundation models, but they can still have the expertise needed to apply AI effectively.

For technology leaders, that shifts the focus to where their best technical talent can create the most value, such as leveraging customer data, aligning AI with business needs, and improving the customer experience.

Skift Research’s State of Travel 2026 report identifies a key AI decision for travel operators: what to build internally and what to source from outside partners. Sierra’s view is that the answer lies in a division of labor.

“We like to say that you should rent the intelligence but own the relationship with your customers,” Zahnlecker said. Travel companies, he added, should retain control of what differentiates them, including their data, customer relationships, operations, brand, and customer experience.

Customer context can become part of that differentiation. An agent that remembers a previous conversation can pick up where it left off, while knowledge of a traveler’s preferences can help shape a more relevant offer. The open question is whether maintaining the infrastructure underneath creates a comparable advantage.

Foundation-model fees may be one of the smaller costs of an internal build, Zahnlecker said. The higher costs can be people and time, particularly when a project takes months to reach production. Sierra occasionally sees companies spend six to 12 months pursuing an internal build before returning to the market for a partner, he said.

For companies that choose to partner, Zahnlecker said the evaluation should focus on whether the technology works in production, whether the company can operate it independently, and whether the commercial model aligns incentives.

A partner should be able to demonstrate that its technology works with the company’s own systems, customers, and traffic patterns. “Prove that it works in my world, with my APIs, with my customers, with my spikiness,” Zahnlecker said.

The travel company’s own team should also be able to use the platform to build and scale agents without relying on the vendor for every change. And Zahnlecker argues that the commercial model should align the provider’s incentives with the customer’s results. Sierra uses outcome-based pricing, meaning it is compensated when an agent delivers a defined result rather than based primarily on technology consumption.

Together, those criteria help technology leaders separate the capabilities that create competitive advantage from the infrastructure that simply needs to work reliably at scale.

#6127. Citi AAdvantage Business Card Loyalty Points Double Dip Explained

The single best way to earn American AAdvantage Loyalty Points with credit card spending often flies under the radar, so I’d like to talk a little more about that in this post, especially since this tends to cause some confusion. Furthermore, this was recently made an “official” card perk, rather than something that just unofficially applied to most cardmembers.

Link: Double dip your Loyalty Points earning with the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard®

With the American AAdvantage Loyalty Points program, you can typically earn one Loyalty Point per dollar spent on a co-branded American credit card. However, there’s one card that’s an exception, and by far the best.

The Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® (learn more) is the co-branded Citi and American Airlines business card. There’s a quirk to the card, though, when it comes to authorized user rewards. On the surface, the authorized user ordinarily earns the Loyalty Points for their spending, and not the primary cardmember, which is an unusual policy for a small business card.

However, through December 31, 2028 (and it’s possible this will be extended again, as it has been in the past), both the primary cardmember and the authorized user earn Loyalty Points for authorized user spending. It basically means you earn two Loyalty Points per dollar spent, just in different accounts. Just to be abundantly clear here:

So the key is for the spending to be on the authorized user’s card, so that this spending unlocks double Loyalty Points (spread across two accounts).

Either way, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card offers several valuable perks, and also has an excellent welcome bonus, making it a good time to apply. So if you are eligible, I’d consider applying even if the double Loyalty Points opportunity doesn’t work out (though hopefully it does).

Personally, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card Loyalty Points double dip is how I qualified for AAdvantage elite status last year. I had a hard time justifying putting spending onto co-branded American cards compared to some other cards out there, when I was only earning one Loyalty Point per dollar.

But if I can qualify for elite status for two people at once, and earn the corresponding Loyalty Point Rewards perks, the math on that spending starts to look much better:

For example, earning 250,000 Loyalty Points per account could potentially earn you a combined total of 12 systemwide upgrades or 170,000 bonus miles. That’s a pretty substantial reward, beyond just the miles you earn for spending and the status!

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card offers an easy opportunity to double dip Loyalty Points earning through authorized user spending. This opportunity is available to all cardmembers, and is currently valid through December 31, 2028 (though has the potential to be extended beyond that). This is a great opportunity, so if you’re pursuing AAdvantage elite status, I’d highly recommend this method.

Have you been taking advantage of this Loyalty Points double dip opportunity?
